references.text: First time in the same scene where the disciples are confused by Jesus' words, creating the context for their exchange of glances in verse 22.
Describes the concrete action where the disciples look at each other to figure out whom Jesus is talking about, and how a specific disciple (John) is asked to inquire.
A parallel account in Matthew's Gospel where the disciples are equally amazed and ask one another who will betray Jesus.
Mark's version of the same event where the disciples look at each other in amazement over Jesus' claim that one of them will betray him.
Luke's account that the disciples began to ask one another which of them it could be who would do this.
